rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable jaundice in itch with no rash
rule_level_problems.problem: Jaundice is gated on (no Severe dry skin) and (no New medication commenced), as the flowchart orders the branches. A patient with itch and yellow skin/eyes who also has very dry skin, or recently started a medication, never gets probable jaundice. Jaundice is the most serious cause on the page (-> page 94), and a drug can itself cause cholestatic jaundice. The rule is faithful to the page's layout, but the sequential gating suppresses a high-value diagnosis. A clinician should confirm whether yellow skin/eyes should override the earlier branches.

summary: The rules encode the page's flowchart faithfully: exclusions, very-dry-skin branch, new-medication branch and jaundice branch, with sound SNOMED choices and no check_for item left unused. The most consequential issue is that jaundice is reachable only when dry skin and new medication are both absent, so a jaundiced patient on either earlier branch is missed. Smaller gaps: the 'in the weeks before the itch' time window for medication is lost, ichthyosis is not represented, and the Itching anchor is not a recorded common symptom.
